subject.title: [Bug]: claude-cli backend SIGKILLs entire process tree at turn end — Workflow / background tool orphans have no opt-out

question: Should claude-cli turn-end cleanup remain fail-closed for the whole CLI process tree, or should OpenClaw add a bounded defer/opt-out path when Claude-native background grandchildren are still running?
rationale: The source and shipped release confirm the reported kill path, but changing it affects orphan prevention, process cleanup safety, config surface, and whether native Claude tools may outlive a normal OpenClaw turn.

options.title: Add bounded defer plus telemetry
options.body: Skip turn-end live-session cleanup only when reliable in-flight background-child evidence exists, cap the drain window, and log/surface pending child state before any forced cleanup.

options.title: Telemetry only
options.body: Keep fail-closed cleanup semantics but snapshot/log process-tree grandchildren and surface a parent-visible failure signal so silent drops become diagnosable.

options.title: Keep current cleanup
options.body: Treat Claude-native background work as unsupported under OpenClaw-managed claude-cli turns and document that durable work must use OpenClaw exec/process or external orchestration.

recommendation.title: Add bounded defer plus telemetry
recommendation.body: Skip turn-end live-session cleanup only when reliable in-flight background-child evidence exists, cap the drain window, and log/surface pending child state before any forced cleanup.
